text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: p99 latency for /v1/generate exceeded 3.5s (5m window) in us-west-2. Paging oncall.
Alex: seeing it on our end as well. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~450ms, p99 jumping to 3-6s. No surge in errors.
Taylor: spike started ~4m after a runtime deploy to runtime-service-canary. Could be KV cache warmup.
Morgan: streaming sessions report stalls — clients get partial frames then time out. Example trace IDs: 0f3a2b, 7c9f11.
Sarah: I'm oncall. quick impact check: any customers with muted retries or 5xx? what about Dedicated pools?
Alex: no 5xx spike. One enterprise customer reported higher tail latency via support ticket 7892.
Raj: infra quick check: node-27 in mgmt-pool showing high iowait and GPU memory pressure around the same time.
Priya: model-side: cache miss rate doubled on kv-cache for redwood-medium-1 after canary. Could amplify token latency.
Taylor: scoreboard from grafana: `inference.latency.p99{route="/v1/generate"}` pinned to pod infer-12 and infer-27. kernel steal ~22% on infer-27.
Alex: running quick flamegraphs on the hot pod now. also checking network: ENI errors none, but pod-to-pod RTTs spike occasionally.
Morgan: streaming stall pattern looks like stalled write syscalls on runtime -> backpressure. Might be batching queue bloated.
Sarah: mitigation options: (1) divert traffic off canary to stable, (2) scale up warm pool, (3) enable degraded streaming mode for affected customers, (4) rollback canary.
Raj: I can scale warm pool +3 nodes in us-west-2 now. Doing `infractl scale pool warm-usw2 +3` — will take ~90s.
Taylor: I can flip routing to exclude runtime-service-canary for critical routes: `routectl set weight runtime-service-canary 0 --routes=/v1/generate`
Alex: while we scale, let's enable model fallback for streaming to `redwood-small-1` for non-production customers to reduce pressure. Priya can toggle.
Priya: enabling fallback for non-prod routes now. patch:
```
api:
  routes:
    - path: /v1/generate
      fallback_model: redwood-small-1
      fallback_condition: latency>2000
```
Priya: applied. non-prod traffic should start falling back within 30s.
Morgan: checked logs after fallback: stalls reduced on non-prod sessions, but p99 still high for prod.
Raj: warm pool nodes are registering and joining. autoscaler reported spikiness in scheduling because of GPU memory fragmentation, but new nodes look healthy.
Taylor: I set canary weight=0 for the affected route. monitoring panels now.
Alex: after routing change + scale + fallback, p99 trending down: 3.8s -> 1.1s -> 420ms over the last 6 minutes.
Sarah: good. keep monitoring for 15m. I'll start incident notes and page SRE for a deeper infra check. @Raj you'll lead infra follow-up, @Priya model-side.
Raj: will take post-incident triage: look into kernel steal, GPU memory fragmentation, and node autoscaler tuning.
Priya: will investigate KV cache warming pattern and whether canary altered cache keying/serialization.
Morgan: opening an incident ticket: INC-2026-114 with timeline and actions. adding logs and traces (IDs above).
Alex: quick customer comms: notify affected customers that mitigation applied and we're investigating root cause. I can draft message.
Sarah: handoff: I'm leaving once p99 stays <700ms for 20m. @Taylor you're next oncall for detailed rollback/rollforward decisions.
Taylor: ack. I'll create a follow-up runbook entry for streaming degradation and canary cache warmup checks.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-114 created and assigned to incidents. Oncall handoff recorded: Sarah -> Taylor.
Sarah: closing the page for now, keeping the Slack thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
